stem: Bromine reacts with methylbenzene in the dark in the presence of a suitable catalyst to form $\text{HBr}$ and compound $\mathbf{L}$, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{Br}$. $\mathbf{L}$ is one of three isomers that can form in this reaction.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
The mechanism for the reaction involves methylbenzene reacting with a $\text{Br}^+$ ion. This ion is produced when bromine reacts with the catalyst.

Complete the equation for the reaction of $\text{Br}_2$ with the catalyst.

$$\text{Br}_2 + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \text{Br}^+ + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
One of the isomers of $\mathbf{L}$ forms in much smaller amounts than the other two isomers.

Draw the structure of this isomer and explain why it forms in the smallest amount.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Complete the mechanism in Fig. 8.1 for the reaction between methylbenzene and the $\text{Br}^+$ ion.

Include all relevant curly arrows and charges.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 8.1

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Chlorobutane and chlorobenzene are added separately to samples of warm aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$.

One of the chloro-compounds reacts slowly and the other does **not** react.
parts.text: Identify the chloro-compound that reacts and describe any observations.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write **two** equations to explain any observations in **(b)(i)**.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain the difference in reactivity of chlorobutane and chlorobenzene with warm aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$.
